title: ResultSetV1
description: The rows a validated plan actually returned, streamed to the browser as a named SSE frame and consumed by the eval harness from the same stream. trace_event.v1 carries row_count but never the rows themselves: a trace records what happened, and every event is persisted, so putting result data there would bloat every stored timeline. This is the answer; that is the story of getting to it.

run_id.description: Identifier of the agent run that produced these rows

columns.description: The result columns in selection order. Row cells are positional against this list, so its length is the width of every row.

rows.description: The rows carried on this frame. May be shorter than row_count when the frame hit its byte budget — see truncated. Cells are positional against columns.

row_count.description: How many rows the executor actually read, after the plan's enforced LIMIT. This is the honest count even when rows carries fewer, so a truncated frame never understates the result.

truncated.description: True when rows carries fewer entries than row_count because the frame exceeded the runtime's result byte budget. The UI must say so rather than presenting a partial table as complete.

elapsed_ms.description: Milliseconds the execution itself took, measured against the injected clock

schema_fingerprint.description: Fingerprint of the database schema these rows were read under, matching the plan's. Lets a cached or replayed result be told apart from one read against a changed schema.

name.description: Column name as the driver reported it

type.description: Declared type as the driver reported it, when it reported one. Drivers do not always know — SQLite returns nothing for a computed column — and an absent type is an honest answer where a guessed one would drive the wrong chart at P8.

cell.description: One value. Null is a real SQL result and is preserved rather than coerced to an empty string. Written as an explicit anyOf rather than a type union so the length bound lands on the string branch alone, and so the browser's validator can keep Ajv strict mode on — under a type union it would need allowUnionTypes, which switches the check off for every schema, not just this one.
